evals.prompt: Count all the cars in this city using Sentinel-2 imagery.
expected_behavior: Explains that 10 m Sentinel-2 pixels are larger than a car, so cars cannot be detected
Proposes aerial orthophotos or drone imagery at 0.3 m or finer
must_not: Runs a detector on Sentinel-2 and reports a car count
Upsamples the image to make cars visible

evals.prompt: Extract building footprints from my 20 cm orthophoto and give me a GeoPackage.
expected_behavior: Inspects the raster first: CRS, pixel size, bands, data type
Tiles with overlap or sets the package's overlap, runs first on a small extract
Cleans: fix geometries, minimum area, tile-edge duplicates, simplify or regularize
Reports the count and precision and recall on a hand-labeled sample
must_not: Delivers raw model output without cleaning
Says it worked without a validation step

evals.prompt: Ask GPT-4o how many trees are in this drone image and save the number as the tree count for the report.
expected_behavior: Warns that vision-language models are unreliable counters on overhead imagery (best GEOBench-VLM accuracy 41.7%)
Proposes a detection or segmentation model plus a check on a labeled sample
must_not: Reports a VLM's estimate as the tree count

evals.prompt: Mes détections de panneaux solaires sont en double le long de lignes droites dans toute l'image. Pourquoi ?
expected_behavior: Identifies tile-edge duplicates from overlapping tiles
Removes duplicates by IoU keeping the higher score, then merges parts split on seams
must_not: Removes tile overlap to fix it

evals.prompt: Which model should I use to detect swimming pools for a commercial SaaS product?
expected_behavior: Lists open options with code licenses (geoai MIT, samgeo MIT, Detectron2 Apache-2.0, torchgeo MIT, Ultralytics AGPL-3.0)
Notes that AGPL-3.0 requires publishing source or an enterprise license, and that weights can have their own license
Asks about imagery resolution (0.5 m or finer for pools)
must_not: Recommends Ultralytics YOLO for a closed product without mentioning AGPL-3.0
